title: Binary Thinking
subject: cs
tagline: Build computer intuition one bit at a time.

lessons.title: Bits as choices
lessons.summary: A bit is not a number first — it is a decision.

steps.title: One bit, two possibilities
steps.body: A light switch is a bit: off or on. Computers store mountains of information by stacking simple yes/no decisions. The power comes from combining many tiny choices.
steps.callout: 0 and 1 are labels for two states — not just small integers.

steps.prompt: How many distinct patterns can 3 bits represent?
Which of these can honestly act like a single bit?

options.label: A dimmer switch with many brightness levels

steps.hint: Look for exactly two clear states — not many.
steps.success: Bits thrive on clean binary decisions.

steps.prompt: Order these from fewest patterns to most patterns.

lessons.title: Place values
lessons.summary: Binary counting uses powers of two instead of tens.

steps.title: Columns that double
steps.body: In decimal, columns are ones, tens, hundreds. In binary, columns are ones, twos, fours, eights… Each step left doubles the place value.

steps.prompt: What decimal value is the binary number 1011?
steps.hint: 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 — turn on the columns with a 1.

steps.prompt: Match each binary pattern to its decimal value.
steps.hint: Find which single place value is switched on.
steps.success: You are reading place value like a computer does.
